app.description: A simple, self-hosted budgeting app for one person.

pageError.title: This page could not be loaded.
pageError.text: Nothing was changed. If LarchBudget was restarting or the connection dropped, trying again usually works.

common.unreachable: Could not reach LarchBudget. Check your connection and try again.

page.title: Transactions
page.lead: Your bank's transactions and the ones you add. Sort each one into a category.
page.emptyNone: No transactions yet. Import a file from your bank, or add one yourself.
page.emptySorted: Everything is sorted. New transactions appear here after your next import.
page.deleteQuestion: Delete {{payee}} of {{amount}} on {{date}}? A later import of the same bank file will not bring it back.
page.deleteQuestionNoPayee: Delete this transaction of {{amount}} on {{date}}? A later import of the same bank file will not bring it back.

summary.narrowed_one: {{count}} transaction matches. Money in {{in}}, money out {{out}}.
summary.narrowed_other: {{count}} transactions match. Money in {{in}}, money out {{out}}.

picker.label: Category for {{what}}, {{amount}}
picker.suggestedTitle: Suggested: you chose {{name}} for this payee last time. Not sorted yet.

form.importedTip: As in the bank file. To change it, delete the transaction and add it yourself.

rules.title: Rules
rules.lead: Sort transactions by the words in them. A rule sorts what you import, and what is still to sort when you save it.
rules.empty: No rules yet. A rule sorts a transaction by the words in its payee or note, so a shop you visit often is sorted as soon as you import it.

form.textTip: Capitals and extra spaces do not matter. When more than one rule fits, the one with the most text wins.
form.fromTransaction: Make a rule from this transaction

row.deleteQuestion: Delete the rule "{{text}}"? What it sorted stays where it is.
row.archivedTip: This category is archived, so the rule sorts nothing. Change the rule to use another category.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.lead: Where your money is. Transactions come in through bank imports.
accounts.empty: No accounts yet. Add the accounts your money is in, with what is in them today.

balance.label: Balance
balance.hint: For a credit card you owe money on, enter a negative amount.
balance.onHint: What the account held at the end of that day. Transactions from before that day that you import later are filled in behind it; they do not change this balance.

row.deleteWithTransactions_one: Delete "{{name}}" and its {{count}} transaction? What was spent from it disappears from your categories. This cannot be undone.
row.deleteWithTransactions_other: Delete "{{name}}" and its {{count}} transactions? What was spent from it disappears from your categories. This cannot be undone.

page.title: Import from bank
page.lead: Download your transactions as a CSV file from your bank's website and add it here. Transactions you imported before are skipped, so files may overlap.
page.noAccountClosed: Transactions are imported into an account, and all of yours are closed. Reopen one, or add a new one.
page.noAccountNone: Transactions are imported into an account, and you have none yet.

problems.tooManyRows: This file has too many rows. Export a shorter period from your bank.
problems.tooWide: This does not look like a bank export: its rows are too wide or too long.
problems.tooLarge: This file is too large. Export a shorter period from your bank.
problems.notCsv: This is not a CSV file. Choose CSV when you download from your bank.

choose.dropHere: Drop your bank's CSV file here, or

columns.intro: Check that the columns below were recognised correctly.
columns.introFromLastTime: Read with the settings from your last import into this account.
columns.moneyInTip: For banks that put money in and money out in separate columns. Amount is then the money out.

columns.invert: Spending is shown as positive numbers
columns.notReady: Choose which columns hold the date and the amount.

breakdown.title: How Ready to assign adds up

welcome.text: Welcome to LarchBudget. Start by adding the accounts your money is in. Their balance becomes your money to assign, and then you divide it over categories.

empty.noCategoriesYet: No categories yet. A category is a purpose you set money aside for, such as Rent, Groceries or Holiday. Categories live in groups, so start by naming your first group, for example Fixed costs.
empty.aboutCategories: A category is a purpose you set money aside for, such as Rent, Groceries or Holiday. Categories live in groups, so start by naming your first group, for example Fixed costs.

explain.overspent: Overspent by {{amount}}: assign more to cover it. {{sum}}
explain.nothing: Nothing assigned or spent this month.

archiveConfirm.positive: Archive "{{name}}"? Its {{amount}} goes back to Ready to assign.
archiveConfirm.negative: Archive "{{name}}"? It is overspent by {{amount}}, which then comes out of Ready to assign.

group.deleteWithCategories_one: Delete the group "{{name}}"? Its category will be archived, and the money in it goes back to Ready to assign.
group.deleteWithCategories_other: Delete the group "{{name}}"? Its {{count}} categories will be archived, and the money in them goes back to Ready to assign.

income.title: Income
income.nextMonthHint: Counts for the next month: this is what came in during {{month}}.

archived.restoringTakes: Restoring takes {{amount}} out of Ready to assign.
archived.restoringAdds: Restoring adds {{amount}} to Ready to assign.

assignTargets.need_one: Your target needs {{amount}} more this month.
assignTargets.need_other: Your targets need {{amount}} more this month.

moveMoney.categoryHolds: {{name}} holds {{amount}}; moving more leaves it overspent.
moveMoney.onlyReady: Only {{amount}} is ready to assign; moving more assigns more than you have.
